headline: Choose factors in nondecreasing order to avoid permutations
statement: Return every unordered factorization of n using at least two factors, each between 2 and n-1. Represent a combination in nondecreasing order; combinations may be returned in any order.
intuition: Choose factors in nondecreasing order to avoid permutations. For any factorization, its smallest factor is at most the square root of the remaining product.
approach: Search factors from a minimum allowed factor through sqrt(remaining).
For each divisor f, emit path + [f, remaining//f].
Recurse on the quotient with minimum factor f to allow repeats without decreasing order.
correctness: Every emitted list multiplies to n and has at least two factors. Nondecreasing choices make each unordered factorization unique. Any factorization with at least two factors has a smallest factor no greater than sqrt(remaining), which the loop reaches; recursion enumerates all decompositions of the quotient.
bruteForce: Enumerate sequences of candidate integers and multiply them, generating many permutations and impossible products.

complexity.time: Output-sensitive search; divisor scans cost O(sqrt(r)) per remaining product r
complexity.explanation: Time Output-sensitive search; divisor scans cost O(sqrt(r)) per remaining product r; auxiliary space O(log n) recursion excluding output. Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Keep the same minimum factor after selecting f so repeated factors are legal.
n=1 and primes have no factorizations.
